titleDv: ޤާނޫނު ނަންބަރު 17/2011 (މަސްތުވާތަކެތީގެ ޤާނޫނު) އަށް ... ވަނަ އިޞްލާޙު ގެނައުމުގެ ބިލު
summary: This bill amends the Drug Act (Law No. 17/2011). It amends Article 2 and adds new Articles 3-1 to 3-4, which set up a way of sorting drugs into numbered schedules (Schedules 1 to 4) and listing or de-listing substances, including a temporary listing process with time limits. It then changes or adds definitions in Articles 5, 6, 7, 9 and 10, and adds new Articles 5-1, 10-1 and 10-2. The scans are hard to read, so some details are uncertain. This summary covers the first 12 of 145 pages.
whyItMatters: What counts as a controlled drug, and so what is an offence, depends on these schedules, so changes here decide which substances people can be charged over.
keyProvisions: Clause 1 amends Article 2 of the Act. The explanatory note in the bill lists seven bullet points on the reasons for the changes.
New Article 3-1 sets out when a substance can be treated as a drug, with several alternative conditions.
New Articles 3-2 and 3-3 define Schedules 1, 2, 3 and 4 and how substances are added to or moved between them.
New Article 3-4 covers temporary listing of a substance. Time limits of 14 days and 30 days appear in the process.
Clauses 3 to 9 insert or rewrite definitions in Articles 5 to 10, including new Articles 5-1, 10-1 and 10-2.
The offences and penalties that follow from these schedules are in later pages and were not rendered.
whoIsAffected: People who use, carry, sell or prescribe drugs, health workers, and the police and courts who apply the Act.
statedReasons: The explanatory note lists seven points on why the Drug Act is being amended, including how drugs are defined and sorted. The exact wording could not be read reliably.
